svg.title: Crash After Commit — Why At-Least-Once + Idempotent Recovery Is Safe
svg.text: Failure Scenario: Process Crashes After DB Commit
The worst ordinary timing window in an at-least-once system — and why this design still recovers safely
1. Kafka delivers the event
poll() returns offset N on this consumer's owned partition
2. Redis reserve(event_id, token) succeeds
state → PROCESSING, bounded TTL lease held
3. PostgreSQL transaction commits
processed_events ledger row + business effects + (fraud/outbox if applicable) — all durable now
4. Process crashes — right here
container killed, OOM, host restart — anything, at the worst possible instant
5. Redis complete() never runs
reservation is left stuck at PROCESSING
6. Kafka offset for N is never committed
commit_terminal() is downstream of complete() — it was never reached
— container restarts / a sibling picks up the partition on rebalance —
7. Kafka redelivers offset N
nothing was ever committed past it — at-least-once, exactly as designed
8. Redis reserve() is called again
the stale PROCESSING lease has TTL-expired by now (bounded, short) — a fresh reservation is granted
9. processed_events duplicate guard fires
SELECT by event_id finds the row from step 3 — digest matches → AlreadyPersistedEvent
the handler, business writes, and fraud/outbox path are never re-run
10. Safe recovery
Redis complete() runs now → offset N commits → processing resumes at N+1
business/fraud/outbox effects were written exactly once — the crash cost only a retry, not correctness
Why this recovers safely, not just "usually works"
• At-least-once, by construction: the Kafka offset only advances after Redis complete() —
which only runs after the DB transaction commits. A crash anywhere before that point means redelivery.
• Idempotent, by construction: the processed_events ledger is the durable, independent source of
truth Redis losing its lease (TTL, restart, flush) cannot undermine — a replay is recognized and skipped.
• No double side effects: business writes and the transactional outbox row live in the same
transaction as the ledger row — if the ledger check says "already done," nothing else ever ran twice either.
• Ordering is preserved through the crash: the partition's next offset is still N — a sibling consumer
(or the restarted process) picks up exactly where the durable state actually is, not where Redis thought it was.
Source: services/event_processor/processor.py (reserve/complete placement), persistence/repositories/processed_events.py (the guard)
See docs/architecture/event-lifecycle.svg for the full non-failure path this timeline is a slice of
